Clean. Working tree now only reflects the actual source changes (`package.json` and `package-lock.json` were already modified/untracked before I started).

## Summary

The catalog page was showing "Loading category..." on every click because `getProducts()` ran inside a server-side `Suspense` boundary that had to await an 800ms fetch on each navigation. I moved that data fetch to a client-side cache that's warmed as soon as the home page renders, so by the time a category link is clicked, the data is already there:

- **`lib/categories.ts`** — shared category metadata (slug/label), safe for the client bundle.
- **`lib/catalog-cache.ts`** — a module-level cache + `prefetchCatalog()`/`useCatalogData()` hook (`useSyncExternalStore`), reused for both prefetching and reading.
- **`app/api/catalog/route.ts`** — new endpoint the cache fetches from.
- **`app/page.tsx`** — now a client component that calls `prefetchCatalog()` for every category on mount, before any click.
- **`app/catalog/page.tsx`** / **`catalog-view.tsx`** — the page no longer reads `searchParams` server-side at all (so `/catalog` builds as a static route); the client view reads `category` via `useSearchParams()` and renders straight from the cache.

Verified end-to-end with a headless-browser run against the production build: visiting `/` fires both `/api/catalog` prefetches immediately; clicking a category link updates the URL and renders the heading+products in ~76ms with zero loading flash and no new network request (served from cache); a cold direct visit to `/catalog?category=sale` still correctly shows the brief loading state before resolving. `/catalog?category=...` URLs are unchanged.
